title: Grade 4 CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — General Assessment #1

pages.quiz:
CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #1
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which thought is likely to lead to a wrong action? (1 mark)
   A. I will share my lunch
   B. I will thank my teacher
   C. I want to take what is not mine
   D. I will help my friend

2. What does the name Abraham point to? (1 mark)
   A. Shepherd
   B. Wise man
   C. Father of many nations
   D. King of Egypt

3. Who was obedient to his parents at Nazareth? (1 mark)
   A. Balaam
   B. Jonah
   C. Jesus
   D. Samson

4. What lesson can we learn from Joseph's plan? (1 mark)
   A. Spend everything
   B. Take all the food
   C. Ignore the future
   D. Plan and save for hard times

5. Where is the Lord's Prayer found? (1 mark)
   A. Matthew 6:9-13
   B. Acts 2:38
   C. John 3:16
   D. Genesis 1:1

6. What did Samson's set-apart life to God mean he must never do? (1 mark)
   A. Cut his hair
   B. Go to Timnah
   C. Eat honey
   D. Visit his parents

7. What is baptism? (1 mark)
   A. A Christian act of washing with water in the name of Father, Son and Holy Spirit
   B. A journey
   C. A dance
   D. A meal

8. Why does the prayer use "our" and "us"? (1 mark)
   A. Only for adults
   B. We pray together and for others
   C. Only for priests
   D. It is a mistake

9. Which of these is part of the extended family? (1 mark)
   A. A bus driver
   B. A classmate
   C. An uncle
   D. A shopkeeper

10. What is the meaning of "bless" in this story? (1 mark)
   A. To insult
   B. To curse
   C. To speak good things over someone
   D. To ignore

11. Which of these helps us to overcome lying? (1 mark)
   A. Exaggerating
   B. Blaming others
   C. Hiding things
   D. Admitting mistakes quickly

12. How did the crowd treat him at first? (1 mark)
   A. They carried him
   B. They ignored Jesus
   C. They told him to be quiet
   D. They gave him money

13. What does "evangelise" mean? (1 mark)
   A. To build
   B. To plant seeds
   C. To cook
   D. To tell others the good news about Jesus

14. Who did the disciples rebuke? (1 mark)
   A. The Pharisees
   B. The soldiers
   C. The children
   D. The people bringing children

15. A stranger offers you a lift. What should you do? (1 mark)
   A. Give your name
   B. Go with them
   C. Accept
   D. Say no and tell a trusted adult

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. Explain the meaning of Proverbs 25:28. (3 marks)

17. Explain why a child should never blame themselves if they were touched wrongly, and say what they should do. (5 marks)

18. Give two examples of personal information that you should not share online. (2 marks)

19. Explain what Jesus taught in Matthew 5:38-39 and what this teaching does not mean. (5 marks)
pages.answers:
CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #1 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — I want to take what is not mine
   Wanting to take what belongs to others leads to stealing.

2. C — Father of many nations
   God said that he would be a father of many nations.

3. C — Jesus
   Luke 2:51 says Jesus was obedient.

4. D — Plan and save for hard times
   Joseph advised saving in good years.

5. A — Matthew 6:9-13
   Matthew 6:9-13.

6. A — Cut his hair
   A Nazirite did not cut his hair.

7. A — A Christian act of washing with water in the name of Father, Son and Holy Spirit
   Baptism is a sign of new life.

8. B — We pray together and for others
   The prayer reminds us to think of others.

9. C — An uncle
   Uncles are relatives outside the nuclear family.

10. C — To speak good things over someone
   To bless is to ask God's good for someone.

11. D — Admitting mistakes quickly
   Admitting mistakes builds truthfulness.

12. C — They told him to be quiet
   Many rebuked him and told him to be quiet.

13. D — To tell others the good news about Jesus
   Evangelising means sharing the gospel.

14. D — The people bringing children
   They told off those who brought the children.

15. D — Say no and tell a trusted adult
   Never go with strangers.

SECTION B
----
16. (3 marks)
   Answer: A person without self-control is like a city with broken walls, easily attacked and unprotected. Self-control protects us.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for broken walls, 1 for unprotected, 1 for self-control protecting.

17. (5 marks)
   Answer: The person who did wrong is always guilty. A child cannot control an adult or older person who chooses to do wrong. The child should tell a trusted adult, who will believe and protect them, and can call 116 for help.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the person doing wrong being guilty, 1 for the child not being to blame, 1 for telling a trusted adult, 1 for the helper protecting, 1 for the helpline.

18. (2 marks)
   Answer: Home address, school, phone number, passwords, family photos.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

19. (5 marks)
   Answer: Jesus taught that we should not repay evil with evil but respond with peace. It does not mean we must stay in danger or let people harm us. If someone keeps hurting us, we should tell a trusted adult who will protect us.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for not repaying evil with evil, 1 for peace, 1 for not staying in danger, 1 for telling a trusted adult, 1 for a clear explanation.
